text:
Sam: FYI support ticket #78921 — customer reports p99 API latency from eu-central jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms around 10:03 UTC. They saw requests egressing to us-east IPs. attaching their probe output.

Maria: thanks, linking the ticket. do we have any infra changes around that time? autoscaling events? :mag_right:

ops-bot: Alert: edge-pop-eu-central latency spike detected (p99 +650ms) at 2026-03-17T10:02:58Z. Related traces: t=grp-394.

Jon: I skimmed infra logs — no recent deploys. Quick check of our edge-dns logs shows increased NXTTL responses from the regional resolver pool at 10:01-10:04. possible resolver churn.

Lee: Customer sent traceroutes, here's the first hop they captured:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (52.14.23.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.8 ms
 2  203.0.113.45  1.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  54.210.11.5 (us-east-1)  320.4 ms
 5  52.14.23.10  322.1 ms
```

Sam: that looks like a geo-detour to us-east. customer is in Frankfurt. they also attached DNS query history showing intermittent answers pointing to us-east A records.

Jon: can you paste the DNS query sample? also which resolver are they hitting (ISP)?

Lee: ISP resolver is isp-frankfurt.net (203.0.113.45). DNS snippet: 
```
; 10:01:12.123 QUERY example.api.redwood.ai A from 203.0.113.45
; ANSWER: 52.14.23.10 (us-east) TTL=12
; 10:01:13.456 QUERY example.api.redwood.ai A from 203.0.113.45
; ANSWER: 52.120.7.99 (eu-central) TTL=360
```

Maria: small TTLs then longer one — could be our authoritative returning mixed records (split-horizon) during a rollout? or an upstream resolver cache poisoning?

Jon: checked our authoritative logs — no config pushes at that minute. but we did have a transient failover of the eu-pop-anycast pair at 10:00:57 which shifted health checks to a backup that advertises a different egress ASN. that could cause the ISP resolver to see different nearest anycast instance and get a state where the returned A record was us-east.

Sam: customer is impacted, asking for mitigation. recommended quick fixes?

Jon: immediate mitigations: 1) add a temporary DNS override in the eu-central authoritative zone to strongly prefer eu IPs for that customer (short term), 2) rollback the anycast failover if safe, 3) ask ISP to flush cache (lee), 4) put a routing policy to prefer eu-egress for eu prefix.

Lee: I can request ISP cache flush but won't be instant. I'll also add the customer tag and escalate support SLA (we're in enterprise plan).

Maria: ops decision: do a targeted DNS override for hostnames used by this customer + add a temporary geo-affinity policy for their tenant while we root cause. Jon, can you prepare the override? include a TTL of 60s.

Jon: preparing override now. snippet I'm about to push to auth-dns: 
```
A record example.customerX.api.redwood.ai -> 52.120.7.99 TTL=60
```
Pushing in 30s. will monitor p99.

ops-bot: Change recorded: auth-dns override applied for example.customerX.api.redwood.ai by Jon at 2026-03-17T10:07:12Z.

Sam: customer reports partial improvement ~10:09 UTC, p99 down to ~180ms but some requests still hit us-east for older resolver caches.

Lee: updated ticket with mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution. also opening a JIRA to investigate why anycast failover exposed differing egress IP sets (NETENG-4821).

Jon: follow-ups: 1) validate anycast health-check logic (why backup announced different egress set), 2) add monitoring for small-TTL churn on authoritative responses from regional resolvers, 3) plan a fix so failover preserves geo-affinity.

Maria: thanks team. assigning oncall rotation to Jon for deep-dive; set postmortem flag if we hit SLO breach. tagging @networking and @dns. :white_check_mark:

Sam: closing loop with customer now. thanks everyone.
